mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS rate change (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs per month for two consecutive months predicts stronger consumer demand and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200000 and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for UNRATE and CPIAUCSL (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month signals supply-side weakness that amplifies equity risk premium and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant negative relationship with INDPRO declines (p > 0.1 in rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of demand (GDPC1) to capacity utilization (implied by INDPRO) falls below 1.2 for three consecutive months, it indicates underutilized production capacity that supports higher long-term growth expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive when the GDPC1/INDPRO ratio is below 1.2 (robustness check across 1000 permutations).

mechanism_narrative: Sudden spikes in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.4% month-on-month) trigger preemptive rate hikes by the FED, which compress the discount rate and reduce expected equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL spikes are not followed by FEDFUNDS increases (Granger causality test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% for two consecutive months suggests tight labor markets that drive wage growth and support positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant positive relationship with UNRATE declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (implied by HOUST) above 2% indicate strengthening consumer demand, which elevates equity risk premiums and predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 2% in a month and repeats in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when HOUST growth is not followed by SPX outperformance (backtest p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months while the demand gauge (GDPC1) continues to rise, it signals a supply bottleneck that amplifies growth expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rising while INDPRO is flat for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the GDPC1-INDPRO pattern persists without SPX appreciation (robustness across 500 permutations).
